title: Senior Estimator – Civil / Road Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Our client is an Australian business supplying road safety barriers - for roadsides, car parks, schools and other sites - to councils, contractors and construction clients across Australia. The business is led by its General Manager and Operations Manager, who this role reports to directly.

PRIMARY PURPOSE

To independently run the day-to-day estimating and quoting workflow - checking plans against the schedule, taking off quantities, sourcing supplier pricing and working out margins - and to build the kind of trust with management, through accurate work, honest communication and a focus on keeping the client happy, that lets the role take on more of the client-facing side over time.

ABOUT THE ROLE

• A senior, full-time Estimator role at the centre of the quoting process - reviewing customer enquiries, checking supplied plans against the job schedule, and turning that into an accurate, priced quote using the company's own templates and rates.

• Internally, one person currently runs estimating end to end, from enquiry through to submitting the quote to the client. Remotely, this role owns the estimating and quoting engine room - checking plans, sourcing supplier pricing, working out margins and building the quote - while management keeps final client sign-off and quote submission in-house at the start.

• As trust builds over the first few months, there is scope for this role to take on more direct client contact. This is not a sales role, and no commercial decision is made without management's sign-off.

• Trusted to work independently on the estimating and quoting workflow and exercise judgement on scope and pricing questions within agreed rates - but genuinely understanding an instruction, plan or piece of feedback, and asking a clarifying question rather than guessing or agreeing by default, matters more in this role than in most.

• Keeping the client happy sits behind every part of this role - even while quote submission stays with management at the start, the accuracy, turnaround and professionalism of the work behind the scenes is what keeps the client relationship strong.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

▸ Enquiries & Plan Review

• Review new customer enquiries and the plans or drawings supplied for the job

• Check the supplied plans against the job schedule to confirm they match, and flag any differences before quoting rather than assuming

• Request missing photos, information or clarification from management rather than guessing

▸ Takeoffs & Quote Preparation

• Perform takeoffs from civil/road design drawings using Adobe for markup and measurement

• Record and tally quantities in Excel, and build the quote using the company's templates, pricing structure and rates

• Own quote accuracy and turnaround time on the estimating side, with minimal supervision

▸ Pricing & Supplier Coordination

• Source and compare pricing from a couple of different suppliers for each job

• Chase, confirm and follow up outstanding supplier pricing

• Work out margins and the final cost to the business before the quote goes to management

▸ Client Communication (Phased)

• In the early months, prepare the quote for management to review and issue to the client directly - client-facing communication and quote submission stay in-house at the start

• Communicate with suppliers directly as required, using the company's official email

• Flag anything a client mentions that could be a new opportunity back to management, even though this is not a sales role

• Over time, and only as agreed with management, take on more direct client contact - by email first, and potentially by phone later

▸ Communication & Judgement

• Ask a clarifying question rather than guessing or agreeing to an instruction, plan or piece of feedback that isn't fully understood - the single most important trait for this role

• Communicate clearly and accurately in written and spoken English with management and suppliers

• Escalate only genuine exception

Who We Are
Evergreen Nephrology partners with nephrologists to transform kidney care through a value-based, person-centered, holistic, and comprehensive approach to kidney care. We believe patients living with kidney disease deserve the best care. We are committed to improving patient outcomes and improving quality of life by delaying disease progression, shifting care to the home, and accelerating kidney transplants.
We help nephrologists focus on the right patients at the right time across the full care spectrum. We do this by providing them with the best-in-class interdisciplinary clinical resources, analytical insight and tools, and services to patients. We listen to the needs of our patients, our employees, and our client partners, continually working to push beyond the status quo in which the care system manages patients today.
Who You Are
You are devoted, compassionate, and enjoy being on the front lines of healthcare, changing the lives of patients by supporting them and the team by focusing on customers. You’re excited about being part of a team that is building a healthcare delivery model that ensures the highest possible quality of life and best outcomes for those in our care. You believe people living with kidney disease deserve the best person-centered, holistic, comprehensive care and want to influence the healthcare system to drive towards that. You thrive in innovative and evolving environments with high rates of change.
Your Role
As a Telephonic Pharmacy Care Coordinator with Evergreen, you play a critical patient-facing and operational role in our pharmacy program. This is a 6-month contract with the opportunity to convert to full-time employment. This program connects patients with a specialized mail-order pharmacy that provides pre-sorted, multi-dose medication packaging (pill packs) along with proactive refill management and periodic care team check-ins, helping ensure patients stay on track with complex medication schedules. Working fully remotely by phone, you are often the first voice patients hear from the pharmacy care team - helping establish trust, explain the value of the pharmacy service, and guide patients through enrollment.
You work with patients from our partner practices to engage them, capture consent, and set up timely access to medications and pharmacist-led clinical services. Your primary focus is high-volume outbound outreach to patients who do not have an office visit, or who cannot be supported onsite, along with inbound support as needed.
This role is focused on telephonic patient engagement, consent and enrollment, EHR documentation, and care coordination for patients living with chronic kidney disease and other complex chronic conditions. Success depends on your ability to connect with patients quickly over the phone, communicate value clearly, and remove the barriers that keep patients from staying consistent with their medications.

Headquartered in Ottawa, BTA Design Services supports the electronic design community across Canada and internationally, specializing in ASIC and FPGA design, verification, and embedded software development. We strengthen our clients' engineering teams and accelerate the delivery of complete, production ready designs.

We are adaptable, efficient, and built around exceptional technical talent. Our continued growth reflects the trust our clients place in us, and we are currently searching globally for a Senior Physical Design Engineer with deep expertise in place and route.

You will join BTA Design Services as an employee and work on behalf of one of our clients, an industry leader building advanced silicon platforms for next generation AI infrastructure. The work pairs leading edge CMOS design with the bandwidth and power demands of modern AI, and the client partners with the world's foremost foundries to bring frontier designs to production. Further details are shared with candidates under confidentiality during the interview process.

This engagement places you at the center of that work, delivering world-class ASICs on the most demanding technology nodes in the industry.
About the Position
As a Senior Physical Design Engineer, you will own backend implementation from netlist to GDSII on challenging blocks and sub-systems. You will apply advanced flows and techniques on single-digit FinFET technology nodes, working alongside a strong and experienced team to bring complex designs to closure. This is a senior, fully remote role, and you may be located anywhere.
Key Responsibilities

• Run place and route implementation flows and analyze the results.

• Create effective floorplans that support physically aware synthesis.

• Drive designs to timing closure and run physical verification.

• Debug issues spanning tools, timing constraints, DFT, and design.

• Partner with the design team to improve RTL and make it implementation friendly.

• Implement and apply timing ECOs.

• Run PrimeTime and analyze timing reports.

• Develop strategies to optimize power and area.

• Run IR-drop analysis and identify optimal strategies to improve it.

• Interface with analog and front-end teams to align on shared objectives.

• 8 or more years of relevant experience in ASIC digital place and route.

• Practical experience with floorplanning.

• Solid grasp of CTS concepts and the ability to design clocks to meet timing requirements.

• Working knowledge of IR-drop optimization strategies.

• Experience with timing closure and ECO implementation (PT-ECO or Tweaker experience is an asset).

• Strong scripting skills.

• Exposure to several of the following: synthesis, StarRC, PT DMSA, RedHawk, Calibre, and formal verification (LEC or Formality).

• A track record as a self-starter who also works well within a team.

Remote Work
This role is fully remote and open to candidates in any location. You will collaborate with distributed engineering teams across time zones, so strong written communication, self-direction, and the discipline to deliver independently are essential.
Why Work With Us
We offer challenging, stimulating technical work with companies that lead the world in technology and innovation. At BTA Design Services , we know our strength lies in the people who join us, so we foster an environment where everyone is trusted, valued, and engaged. We also believe work-life balance matters, and we give our engineers demanding, rewarding roles while leaving room for family, friends, and life beyond work. This is a new position. title: Mid-Level Software Engineer – C#
description:
ABOUT VICTORY LIVE
Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory. We provide an end-to-end software platform for the live ticketing industry, managing thousands of sports, theater, and live music event tickets on behalf of artists, promoters, teams, venues, and professional resellers. Victory Live ’s comprehensive offerings include an established B2B marketplace, along with both a full-service and an automated SaaS platform to handle all elements of the ticket sales lifecycle, from ingestion to sales fulfillment.
THE POSITION
Victory Live is looking for a Mid-Level Software Engineer to build and maintain features across our C# and .NET services. You'll own well-scoped pieces of our B2B marketplace and ticketing platform end to end, from design through production, working closely with senior engineers who'll help you level up.
RESPONSIBILITIES

•
Ship features. Build and maintain services in ASP.NET Core, from a scoped design through code review to production.

•
Write tests that hold. Cover your code with xUnit so regressions show up in CI, not in production.

•
Debug production issues. Use logs, metrics, and Datadog dashboards to trace bugs to root cause.

•
Work within our data layer. Write efficient Entity Framework Core queries and migrations that don't lock production tables.

•
Handle messaging and background work. Build and monitor jobs on RabbitMQ or Kafka.

•
Take code review seriously. Review teammates' PRs and act on the feedback you get on your own.

•
Use AI tooling daily. Pair with Claude Code and Copilot for scaffolding, tests, and debugging, and learn where to trust them and where not to.

REQUIREMENTS

• 2-4 years building production software, with at least 1-2 years in C# and .NET.

• Comfortable building REST APIs with ASP.NET Core.

• Solid grasp of xUnit (or NUnit) and test-driven development.

• Working knowledge of Entity Framework Core, SQL Server, and relational databases.

• Growing but genuine use of AI tooling in your day-to-day workflow.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Exposure to RabbitMQ, Kafka, or other messaging systems.

• Familiarity with Redis or Azure services.

• Interest in ticketing, marketplaces, or high-transaction consumer platforms.

WHY VICTORY LIVE

• You'll build the infrastructure live events run on; millions of tickets, hundreds of venues, many of the largest teams and events in the world.

• A lean team where decisions move fast and your code reaches real fans, often the same week.

• Every release has stakes. Every improvement is felt.

• High expectations, low tolerance for politics, and a culture built on writing well and shipping with care.

OUR VALUES
We build the systems that power live event ticketing, and we hold a high bar for how we do it. Four principles run through everything:

•
Quality of life. Sustainable processes over heroics. Nobody should be a single point of failure, and nobody should be afraid to take a vacation.

•
Quality of code. Clarity over cleverness. If a teammate needs a long explanation to follow your code, it needs simplifying. Tests prove your work; they aren't optional.

•
Protection of production. Every change is reviewed, tested, and observable. We build with monitoring in mind from day one so we find problems before our users do.

•
Shared knowledge. We work across time zones, so we communicate in the open. Questions go in channels, not DMs, and one answer becomes shared knowledge.

ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
We are an AI-native engineering team. Here is what that looks like in practice:

•
AI-assisted engineering. Every engineer uses Claude, Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic tooling as a routine part of their workflow.

•
Async-first. Most decisions happen in writing through Jira, Confluence, PR descriptions, design docs. We over-communicate on changes and under-communicate on noise.

•
Ownership mindset. Engineers are responsible for what they write and no code

This is a hands-on sales role focused on identifying freight opportunities, connecting with shippers and logistics decision-makers, and helping get Spotter's 600-truck fleet into new freight opportunities.
You will work closely with our sales, operations, and pricing teams to identify qualified opportunities and turn them into lanes, bids, pilots, and recurring freight.
Initial Market Focus
This hire will initially focus on local work around Joliet, IL and long-haul freight leaving the Joliet, IL area.
What You'll Do

• Research and identify potential direct shippers with relevant freight volume.

• Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective shippers in the Joliet market.

• Reach out to transportation, logistics, and procurement contacts.

• Identify upcoming RFPs, mini-bids, pilots, and truckload opportunities .

• Help prospective shippers complete carrier onboarding and qualification processes.

• Introduce Spotter's 600-truck capacity to qualified freight opportunities.

• Follow up consistently with prospects and move opportunities toward a concrete next step.

• Work with operations and pricing to determine which lanes Spotter can service and price.

• Maintain accurate pipeline and account information in our CRM.

• Help develop direct-shipper relationships that can grow into recurring freight.

What We're Looking For

• Previous experience in freight sales, transportation, logistics, brokerage, 3PL, or a related field is a plus.

• Strong communication and prospecting skills.

• Comfortable with outbound calls, email outreach, and LinkedIn prospecting.

• Understanding of FTL / truckload transportation is a plus.

• Ability to identify and qualify potential freight opportunities.

• Strong follow-up and organization skills.

• Comfortable using CRM systems and transportation technology.

• Self-motivated and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.

• Willingness to learn direct-shipper sales and freight procurement .

Experience with shipper RFPs, carrier onboarding, TMS platforms, digital freight platforms, or transportation procurement is a plus.

Success in this role means consistently building a qualified pipeline of direct-shipper opportunities and moving prospects toward carrier onboarding, RFPs, bids, pilots, and awarded lanes.
You will be measured primarily on qualified opportunities and tangible pipeline progress , rather than simply the number of calls or emails completed.
Why Spotter
Spotter operates a 600-truck asset base , giving you the opportunity to sell real transportation capacity and develop direct relationships with shippers.
You'll have the opportunity to learn enterprise freight procurement, direct-shipper sales, and contract truckload , while growing into larger strategic accounts as you demonstrate results.

Our mission is to architect AI that learns from and interacts with the world like humans do.

We're pioneering the model architectures that will make this possible. Our founding team met as PhDs at the Stanford AI Lab, where we invented State Space Models or SSMs, a new primitive for training efficient, large-scale foundation models. Our team combines deep expertise in model innovation and systems engineering paired with a design-minded product engineering team to build and ship cutting edge models and experiences.

We're funded by leading investors at Index Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners, along with Factory, Conviction, A Star, General Catalyst, SV Angel, Databricks and others. We're fortunate to have the support of many amazing advisors, and 90+ angels across many industries, including the world's foremost experts in AI.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Cartesia builds real-time multimodal intelligence: fast, state-of-the-art voice models and the products that make them useful. We started as a research lab, pioneered the state space model architecture, and now we're bringing that research to customers through intuitive tools for creating, testing, and shipping with voice.

In this role, you'll build the product experiences around Cartesia's models. You may work across Voices, Playground, and other core surfaces as priorities evolve. You'll own work end-to-end and directly shape the quality, usability, and developer experience of how customers discover our models, understand what they can do, and put them into production.

YOUR IMPACT

- Build polished, intuitive experiences across Voices, Playground, and adjacent product surfaces, turning powerful model capabilities into workflows customers can understand and use.

- Own customer problems end-to-end, from discovery and prototyping through implementation, launch, measurement, and iteration.

- Improve the speed and confidence with which customers can evaluate, configure, and integrate Cartesia's voice models.

- Define how product quality is measured, building analytics, evaluations, experiments, and regression tracking that reveal where experiences succeed or break down.

WHAT YOU BRING

- Experience building and operating customer-facing software in production, ideally at a high-growth startup. We care more about what you've shipped than strict years of experience.

- Strong product instincts: you think in customer outcomes, usability, quality, and developer experience, and you have opinions on what to build and why.

- Full-stack range and the ability to own a product surface across frontend, backend, APIs, data, and operational concerns.

- Fluent use of coding agents and a habit of keeping pace with the frontier.

- Clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences, strong cross-functional partnership, and a sharp presence in product and design reviews.

NICE-TO-HAVES

- Experience building developer tools, creative tools, playgrounds, or API-adjacent products.

- Experience building AI-powered products and translating model capabilities, limitations, and quality tradeoffs into understandable user experiences.

- Strong frontend craft with React and TypeScript, including polished, highly interactive workflows.

- Experience with audio, media, real-time systems, product analytics, experimentation, or evaluation infrastructure.

title: Technical Architect II - AI-Native
description:
Overview
The AI-Native Technical Architect II provides advanced architectural leadership within an assigned business area, aligning solution development with broader architecture direction while remaining closely connected to implementation. This role translates business and product intent in alignment with architectural direction into clear, implementable specifications that orchestrate AI agents and engineering workflows to produce delivery-ready solutions across applications, services, APIs, data flows, and platform components.
As a senior technical leader, the AI-Native Technical Architect II drives architecture for their business area, establishes and applies technical standards within their scope, and guides traditional teams and AI-native pods through design trade-offs involving cost, scalability, security, reliability, and maintainability. The role is expected to balance strategic thinking with hands-on technical depth, applying strong systems thinking to ensure architecture decisions consider end-to-end flows, dependencies, and long-term platform evolution while being effectively realized in code and operational outcomes.
This role operates within a complex, regulated healthcare domain and is expected to either bring deep domain expertise or quickly develop a strong understanding of healthcare data, workflows, and compliance considerations, ensuring that architecture decisions are grounded in real-world business and regulatory constraints.
In the AI-native model, the Technical Architect II treats AI as both a solution capability and an engineering accelerator. This includes designing software that incorporates AI-enabled features where appropriate and advancing AI-assisted and agent-based development practices, including code generation, automated testing, intelligent engineering workflows, and reusable AI skills. The Technical Architect II plays a key role in helping teams apply AI effectively and responsibly, ensuring outputs are correct, secure, maintainable, and aligned to architectural intent through clear human accountability and guardrails.
The role partners with senior architects, enterprise architecture, and shared AI and Data teams when broader alignment is needed, while owning architectural execution and ensuring teams utilize modern AI-native approaches efficiently and correctly within the assigned business area.

•

title: iOS Software Engineer

Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.
Role
As an iOS Software Engineer, you own the iOS client experience, how AI feels, responds, and performs in users’ hands. This is not a thin integration role. Focus

• Integrate AI-powered features through backend APIs.

• 3+ years of iOS development experience using Swift.

• Hands-on experience integrating AI-powered features into mobile apps.

• Strong understanding of async/await, concurrency, and background tasks.

• Solid iOS performance and memory optimization skills.

• Experience shipping and maintaining production iOS apps.

• Comfort designing for latency, partial failure, and non-deterministic AI behavior.

• Familiarity with feature flags or remote configuration systems.

• Strong intuition for AI UX patterns and user trust considerations.

• Stable, smooth, and reliable real-world use iOS applications.

Tech Stack

• Swift

• SPM

• SwiftUI

• SQL / noSQL

• TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

How We Work
The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

About Lokal
In 2018, we began with a WhatsApp group with a simple hypothesis: people in tier-2/3 towns weren’t really using the internet meaningfully yet. We believed that if we started with local content in their own language, they’d come back every day; once there was a habit and trust, that same space could naturally grow into classifieds and, eventually, something they used for almost everything online. This spark became Lokal . Our first instinct was to put everything in one place & one app - local updates, classifieds, jobs, matrimony and more. It worked, till it stopped working. Users gave us the insight - when one use case outweighs the others, everything else seems like noise. We listened. Like how Craigslist quietly seeded a generation of focused companies & marketplaces, we began unbundling and verticalising.
Today, Lokal is a house of focused apps, many products, one mission:
to connect Tier-2/3+ India to the Knowledge, opportunities, tools and experts they’ve always deserved.
We now operate dozens of live apps across categories like:

• Edutainment & Skill Learning - practical skills and learning in regional languages (GyanTV)

• Matrimonial Matchmaking - hyperlocal, compatibility-first partner search ( Lokal Matrimony)

• Agri Consulting - farmer-first advisory in local languages (Agri Lokal )

• Local Jobs - blue- and grey-collar opportunities close to home ( Lokal Jobs)

• Social & Community - Place to find & post social updates ( Lokal app)

• Emotional Well-being & Peer Support - safe spaces to talk and feel heard (Dostt & Eaze)

• Astrology & Guidance - instant access to trusted Astrologers via chat and voice (Astro Lokal )

• Advisory Services - early bets in legal help, financial guidance, career counselling, and more

Under the hood, Lokal is a discovery and access platform: local-language internet + deep Bharat insight+ AI. When someone opens a product we’ve built, they don’t wade through clutter; they get a straight line to what they came for.
This is the story new teammates walk into:
a company that started as a whatsapp group, became a family of focused apps, and kept one belief at the centre - access changes lives .

We ship fast. We learn fast. We build for Bharat.
We are backed by leading global and domestic investors including Y Combinator, Sony, Global Brain, India Quotient, and 3one4 Capital.

description:

WorkOS builds modern developer tools and APIs that make it easy for companies to become Enterprise Ready. Our platform powers authentication, identity, authorization, and other critical infrastructure that developers need to securely scale their products to large organizations.

Our fast-growing customer base includes hundreds of modern software companies building the next generation of enterprise-ready products.

ABOUT THE SECURITY PLATFORM TEAM

The Infrastructure Security team provides and supports the primitives that enable engineering to securely build applications and meet compliance obligations, while abstracting away the underlying complexity for the best possible developer experience.

Our work centers on workload identity and authorization: how internal applications authenticate to each other and to the services they depend on, and how that access is granted and enforced. We're replacing static secrets with short-lived identity credentials, bringing identity-based authentication to the services engineers use every day, and unifying how authorization is managed across the company.

- A systems thinker. You reason carefully about bootstrapping, circular dependencies, availability, and failure modes, especially for infrastructure that everything else depends on.

- A pragmatic migrator. You know that shipping the primitive is half the job. You can drive adoption across many teams, meet them where they are, and retire the legacy path.

- A strong partner to engineering. You build trust with engineers by understanding their priorities and making security frictionless.

- Excited about AI. You're embracing AI and automation to scale platform work and reduce toil.

- Curious and humble. You ask the basic questions, enjoy untangling complex systems, and bring others along with you.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Build workload identity infrastructure. Make short-lived identity credentials a default part of every application's runtime environment, in partnership with application platform owners.

- Bring identity-based authentication to internal services. Work with the owners of major internal dependencies to support identity certificates, make them the golden path for newly onboarding applications, and drive migration of existing ones.

- Eliminate static secrets. Replace all static passwords and service tokens with short-lived identity credentials, and build identity-authenticated egress proxies and API abstractions that inject and automatically rotate managed secrets for the external dependencies that still require them.

- Unify authorization. Build a single interface and framework through which authorization policies are centrally managed and enforced.

description:
WHAT WE'RE RESEARCHING

We're hiring hospitalists and family medicine physicians to help us evaluate the accuracy of clinical AI tools. This research feeds directly into improving how algorithms suggest diagnoses based on patient charts. Your medical expertise will help determine where AI models succeed and where they fall short in real-world clinical scenarios.

You will review a series of de-identified patient records through our remote platform. For each case, you will form your own clinical diagnosis based on the provided chart. Language Associate (Dutch) - Part-Time Position (Approx. 20 hours/week)
This is an exciting consultant position that offers a unique opportunity to support large-scale social change efforts. Language Associates bring Avaaz to millions of people each week by translating Avaaz campaigns from English into key languages and rewriting them to be fitting to local contexts. This role requires strong written communication skills and cultural awareness that allow you to capture the heart of Avaaz ’ campaigns and powerfully translate them into Dutch language.
The successful candidate for this part-time position (20 hours/week) will work closely with the Dutch language lead and with the Member Engagement and Community Petitions teams, and they will report to an Avaaz staffer. Please note that this position is on a freelance/independent contractor basis.
Responsibilities

• Translate Avaaz campaigns from English to Dutch to turn them into strong, emotive, and compelling campaigns to send out in The Netherlands and Belgium, and to Dutch-speaking members around the world.

• Support the Dutch campaign team to write and edit excellent campaign materials such as briefings, advocacy letters, and press releases. Translate and/or edit other materials as necessary: Media material, content for social media etc.

• Reviewing, managing, and supporting the petitions published by Dutch members on the Avaaz Community Petitions website.

Qualifications

• Excellent written and oral communication, and translation skills in Dutch, combined with creative thinking to craft engaging texts.

• Excellent communication skills in English, the Avaaz team’s working language.

• Professionalism, efficiency, and results-oriented delivery on short timelines.

• Flexibility and ability to adapt to (somewhat) varying weekly workloads.

• Passion and commitment to global justice, citizen empowerment, and social change.

• Strong teamwork skills, comfortable in a highly collaborative culture, and a hierarchical team structure.

• Proficient in Google Suite and online communication systems (Slack, Zoom, etc).

• Ideally: cultural and linguistic understanding of regional differences (e.g. the Netherlands and Belgium), to guarantee Avaaz content can be understood across Dutch-speaking regions.

Compensation
This is an independent contractor role, paid at an hourly rate of €25,- depending on experience and location

title: Integrated Marketing Manager, AI Impact
description:
About the Team

Like every team at OpenAI, the Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring that artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We help people understand what AI makes possible through the experiences of the people, communities, and customers using it.

We work closely with Social, Community, Communications, Creative, Production, and other teams to bring those experiences to life. Our work connects human stories with integrated marketing programs that build understanding and inspiration with our key audience.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to identify and curate the strongest proof points of AI’s impact-across people, communities, and society-and turn them into stories and programs that resonate.

You’ll be a builder and storyteller with the curiosity to uncover an extraordinary story and the initiative to make something of it. You’ll seek out people using AI in meaningful ways, build relationships, understand what has changed for them, and help them share their experiences in their own voices.

Working deeply with Social, Community, and Communications, you’ll shape stories together and build the programs, content, and distribution plans that help them travel. That could mean developing a recurring story series, bringing a community’s experience to a national audience, or turning a customer story into a program that invites others to participate.

You’ll combine strong editorial instincts with integrated marketing leadership, taking work from discovery and a clear brief through production, launch, and measurement. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable shaping an ambitious idea, facilitating a conversation with a story participant, and organizing the people and resources needed to bring a program to life.

In this role, you will:

- Find the strongest proof points: Proactively discover people, communities, and customers using AI in meaningful ways. Evaluate the evidence, human significance, and audience relevance behind each opportunity.

- Build alongside Social, Community, and Communications: Partner from the outset on story discovery, creative ideas, programming, and distribution. Align on a shared plan, clear roles, and the right moments to bring stories to audiences.

- Turn stories into programs: Create integrated campaigns, recurring content series, community activations, and partnerships that give strong stories a life beyond a single asset or launch.

- Connect national reach with local relevance: Adapt stories, formats, messengers, and programs to the audiences and communities they serve. Identify when a local story can resonate nationally and how a national program can become meaningful locally.

- Lead work from idea to delivery: Own briefs, creative development, production, timelines, budgets, partner coordination, launch, and optimization across social, owned, earned, experiential, community, and relevant paid channels.

- Champion craft and credibility: Partner with Creative, producers, and agencies to make distinctive, engaging content. Ground stories in demonstrated impact, bring technical ideas to life through human experiences, and represent participants accurately and thoughtfully.

- Build a repeatable approach: Develop a network of internal and external partners and a practical process for sourcing, prioritizing, developing, and sharing stories. Create formats and programs that can grow while leaving room to act on unexpected opportunities.

- Measure what resonates: Set clear goals for audience understanding, reach, engagement, sharing, and participation. Use results and feedback from audiences and participants to improve the stories, formats, and programs we build.

You will thrive in this role if you have:

- Relevant experience: 12+ years in integrated marketing, content or editorial strategy, customer storytelling, community marketing, or related fields, including significant experience leading complex campaigns and programs.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
FORWARD DEPLOYED ENGINEER (ALL GENDERS)

THE OPPORTUNITY

AI is fundamentally changing how the world’s largest enterprises operate.
At Lio, we’re building THE AI workforce for procurement.

We’re now expanding to the US and we’re looking for our first Forward Deployed Engineer in the US to help build Lio’s presence from the ground up.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work at the intersection of Engineering, Product, and enterprise customers. You'll build integrations, solve complex technical challenges, and help turn customer requirements into scalable product capabilities.

This is your chance to join Lio at the very beginning of our US expansion, working directly with Fortune 500 customers and helping shape how we build and scale in the US.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

In this role, you will:

- Build enterprise integrations across APIs, SAP, and other business systems

- Work directly with enterprise customers to design scalable technical solutions

- Debug and resolve complex issues across production environments

- Own customer-driven product features from implementation to production

- Build MVPs and evolve them into scalable platform capabilities

- Automate deployment and implementation workflows with Product and Engineering

- Turn recurring customer needs into reusable product features

- Help establish Lio's FDE function in the US and shape how we serve American enterprise customers as we scale

YOUR PROFILE

You'll thrive in this role if you:

- Enjoy solving technical problems across APIs, integrations, and distributed systems.

- Take ownership. You care about building reliable, scalable solutions-not just getting things to work.

- Like working closely with customers and translating real-world challenges into product improvements.

- Communicate clearly and enjoy collaborating across Engineering, Product, and customer teams.

- Enjoy fast-moving environments where you can learn quickly and have a direct impact.

- Are excited about AI and the opportunity to bring it into enterprise operations.

WHAT'S NOT REQUIRED

Experience with procurement software or SAP isn't required.

We're much more interested in strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, ownership, and your ability to solve complex technical challenges than in having the perfect CV.

WHY JOIN LIO?

Lio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and built at Y Combinator. We're bringing Silicon Valley ambition and engineering culture to Munich.

From day one, you'll work with Fortune 500 companies across Europe and the US, solving real-world technical challenges at the intersection of AI and enterprise software.

We move fast, care deeply about execution, and give engineers ownership from day one. The solutions you build won't stay customer-specific-they'll shape the future of our platform.

If you're excited about building AI systems that run in production at global enterprises, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Support Representative, APAC
description:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems - robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

ABOUT THE ROLE

*Open to hiring in London and APAC.

We're building a creative platform used by artists, filmmakers, and teams at some of the world's most recognized brands. Our support org handles everything from a five-minute billing question to a technical escalation, and we're building out a dedicated tier for the first kind so our more experienced specialists can focus on the second.

We're looking for a Support Representative who's accurate, fast, and comfortable following a process closely under volume. No creative or AI background required. We'll train you on the product.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Resolve high-volume, tickets across account access, billing, and plan questions for Free, Standard, and Pro and Max users

- Use existing macros, playbooks, and AI support layer suggestions to close tickets accurately and quickly

- Recognize when a ticket needs product judgment or creative-tool troubleshooting, and route it to Tier 2 Support or Enterprise

- Flag recurring questions that don't have a macro yet

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

- Clear, accurate written communication, especially on process-driven, checklist-style work

- Comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work without losing accuracy

- Prior experience with tools like Zendesk, Notion, or Slack is a plus, not a requirement

- 0-2 years in any customer-facing or process-driven role (preferably in SaaS, but not required)

- Enough curiosity to spend a little time in the product or help docs before talking to us. No creative background needed, just evidence you looked

WHAT SETS GREAT CANDIDATES APART

The best people in this role follow the playbook precisely and know exactly when a ticket doesn't fit it. They don't force a wrong answer to hit volume, and they don't escalate everything out of caution either. They've put in enough time with Runway to have a real sense of what it does and who uses it, so a ticket that's slightly off-script doesn't stump them, even without a creative background. When they see the same question surface three times, they ask whether it should become a macro instead of just answering it a third time.

title: Principal Infrastructure Architect: Data Platform
description:
ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen-fast.

As a Principal Infrastructure Architect on our Infrastructure Architecture team, you will be the architecture team's partner to ZoomInfo 's data engineering organization. Data engineering owns the platforms and the products built on them. You bring the infrastructure patterns, evaluation rigor, and cross-team alignment that help them build and run those platforms well on GCP.
This is a cloud architect seat with a data specialty. You bring the same cloud, Kubernetes, networking, and infrastructure-as-code foundation as the rest of the architecture team, plus enough hands-on depth in data systems to be credible with the engineers who run them.
The work breaks down four ways:

•
Patterns. You establish and maintain the paved-road patterns data teams build on: infrastructure as code, CI/CD for data jobs and pipelines, monitoring and alerting, performance, and cost. You keep them easy to consume and self-service.

•
Enablement and alignment. You help data teams adopt those patterns, review their designs, and work through hard infrastructure trade-offs with them.

•
Evaluation. You run POCs of new data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process, and you write recommendations engineering leaders can act on.

•
Shared stewardship. You take a full share of the architecture team's general work: weekly architecture reviews across all domains, standards and ADRs, and infrastructure consulting for any team that needs it.

The data estate is broad. We don't expect deep experience across all of it. We expect real depth in some areas and the ability to build depth in others as the work demands. Patterns get adopted here through leadership and communication rather than positional authority. You'll write reference implementations, open the first PRs, and stay hands-on through enablement when a critical initiative calls for it.
What You'll Do

•
Establish infrastructure patterns for data workloads. Design and maintain reference patterns for provisioning and operating the data platforms ZoomInfo runs: streaming and messaging (Kafka/Confluent, Pub/Sub), operational databases (PostgreSQL/Cloud SQL, MongoDB), analytical stores (BigQuery, Snowflake), search (Elasticsearch/Solr), pipeline orchestration and processing (Apache Airflow/Cloud Composer, Dataflow/Apache Beam), and open table formats (Apache Iceberg). Ship them as Terraform modules, GitOps workflows, and documented standards that data teams can adopt without reinventing them.

•
Build the data paved road. Today's delivery tooling is application-centric. Define CI/CD and GitOps patterns for data jobs and pipelines, and partner with platform engineering and data engineering to make data delivery as safe and automated as application delivery.

•
Establish performance, cost, and observability patterns. Give data teams the patterns and guidance to run stores and pipelines efficiently (query and storage optimization, partitioning and clustering, tiering and retention, workload isolation, right-sizing) and the monitoring, alerting, and SLO practices that make performance and cost visible. Set the baseline patterns for backup, restore, and disaster recovery of data stores, including RTO/RPO targets. Partner with FinOps on data-layer spend. Review workloads with teams against these patterns and help them align.

•
Evaluate new technologies. Run structured POCs of emerging data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process. Recent examples include graph and distributed SQL databases, stream processing (Apache Flink, Confluent Flink), and schema management and catalo

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

JOIN US IF YOU WANT TO

1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

In six years, Lendable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

- Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

- Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

- Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

- Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

- Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

- Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

- 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

- You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

- You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

title: Engineering Team Lead
description:
We're currently hiring for remote team members in the following states: DC, DE, GA, MA, MD, NC, NH, NJ, OH, PA, SC, UT, and VA.

We're AWeber , a remote‑first company that helps small businesses around the world form meaningful connections with their customers and grow their businesses using our marketing communication software. We are fanatical about small businesses and we hope you are too!

At AWeber , agentic development is core to how we build. Our engineers spend most of their time designing agents and agentic engineering systems, reviewing agent‑generated work for quality and correctness, and coordinating that work across the codebase. As an Engineering Team Lead, you build a small team of engineers who do exactly that into a high‑performing, healthy, well‑functioning group, and you lead them from inside the work.

This is a player‑coach role. You run 1:1s, grow careers, own hiring and reviews for your team, and own its delivery and quality bar. You also stay hands‑on: designing solutions, reviewing agent output on the risky paths, and shipping the hard parts yourself. We are not looking for someone who leaves the code behind. We are looking for the senior engineer other people already rely on, who leads and grows a team without losing their own hands on the keyboard. Your mission is to help a capable, curious group ship work the org can trust, move quickly without cutting corners, and consistently finish what they start.

On any given day, you could be found reviewing an agent‑generated pull request on a risky path and coaching the engineer on how they verified it, running a 1:1 that turns someone's recurring frustration into an owned initiative, interviewing a candidate and sharpening how your team evaluates new hires, pairing for an hour to unblock a stalled migration, deciding what comes off the plate so your team is not underwater, or carrying your team's priorities into a cross‑team engineering forum.

You'll thrive as an Engineering Team Lead if you

• Lead from inside the work, stay hands‑on in the code, and measure success by your team's output and growth rather than your own.

• Have a bias to action, turning recurring problems into owned, dated, shipped solutions instead of letting good ideas recirculate.

• Treat verification and trust as the real throughput limit in an AI‑first org, and hold the line on quality without stalling momentum.

• Make people decisions and difficult trade‑offs with care, and own the outcomes.

• Establish standards and inspire others, not just through your own expertise but through mentorship and advocacy.

• Default to open, transparent communication, and adapt your message to engineers, peers, product partners, and leadership.

• Stay calm and steady when priorities compete, and keep your team oriented on what matters most.

• Stay a forever learner, and grow the people around you.

Required skills and qualifications

• 7+ years in hands‑on software engineering roles, with real depth on the backend (Python) or the front end (React, TypeScript, or modern JavaScript frameworks), and the judgment to review and improve both engineers' and agent‑generated code.

• 1+ year in a technical lead, team lead, or hands‑on project management role, with a track record of mentoring and growing engineers. We are open to a strong first‑time people manager who has been a de facto lead.

• Experience owning a team's delivery: setting direction, breaking down ambiguous work, holding people accountable to commitments, and driving projects to done.

• Demonstrated ability to design solutions with AI development tools and coding assistants, and to raise a team's standard for reviewing agent‑generated work.

• Strong experience across our stack: Python, React, and TypeScript, plus databases, caching strategies, UNIX development tools, and deploying to AWS or other cloud infrastructure.

​

As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home.
